intro: The .env to JSON converter turns a dotenv-style environment file into a formatted JSON object, parsing each KEY=VALUE line into a key-value pair. It is handy when you need to migrate environment variables into a JSON config, inspect a .env file as structured data, or feed values into tooling that expects JSON. Paste your dotenv content and get a clean, indented JSON object back instantly in your browser.
useCases: Convert a project's .env file into a JSON config object for tooling that reads JSON
Inspect environment variables as structured, readable JSON
Migrate dotenv values into a settings file or seed a secrets-management entry
Quickly strip comments and normalize KEY=VALUE pairs into JSON for review
Generate JSON from environment variables to paste into documentation or examples

faq.q: Is my .env data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser using client-side JavaScript, and nothing is uploaded or stored on any server. Your environment variables and secrets never leave your device.

faq.q: How are comments and blank lines handled?
faq.a: Empty lines and lines starting with # are skipped. Lines without an = sign are ignored as well.

faq.q: Does it support the 'export' prefix used in shell scripts?
faq.a: Yes. A leading 'export ' on a key is stripped, so 'export KEY=value' becomes the key 'KEY' in the output.

faq.q: What happens to quotes around values?
faq.a: If a value is wrapped in matching single or double quotes, the surrounding quotes are removed. The remaining content is kept as-is, without escape-sequence processing.

faq.q: Are all values output as strings?
faq.a: Yes. Every value becomes a JSON string; numbers and booleans are not converted to their JSON types. Duplicate keys keep the last value seen.
